name: Cost of electricity
description: Computes the cost of electricity consumed by multiplying the energy used in kilowatt-hours by the unit price per kilowatt-hour. Using 350 kWh at a price of 27 per kWh costs 9450.
notes: Energy must be in kilowatt-hours and price per kWh; the currency of the result matches the price you enter. Fixed charges and taxes on a real bill are not included.

name: Price incl. tax
description: Adds a tax rate to a base price, computing price×(1+rate/100). The result is the total amount payable including tax.
notes: Enter the tax rate as a percentage number (e.g. 10 for 10%), not as a fraction. The default rate is 10%.

name: Discounted price
description: Applies a discount to a price, computing price×(1−discount/100). The result is the amount paid after the discount is deducted.
notes: Enter the discount as a percentage number (e.g. 20 for 20%). A discount above 100 would give a negative, meaningless price.

name: Tip amount
description: Computes the gratuity as bill×rate/100, the tip amount to add based on the bill total and a chosen tip percentage.
notes: This returns only the tip, not the bill plus tip. Enter the rate as a percentage number; the default is 15%.

name: Markup
description: Computes the markup as the selling price minus cost, divided by cost: (price − cost)/cost. It expresses profit as a fraction of the cost, the basis on which prices are set.
notes: Markup is measured against cost, whereas margin is measured against price, so the two differ. The result is a decimal; multiply by 100 for a percentage.

name: Currency conversion
description: Multiplies an amount in one currency by an exchange rate to obtain the equivalent value in another currency. The rate is the number of target-currency units per unit of the source currency.
notes: Make sure the rate is quoted in the intended direction (target per source); an inverted rate gives a very wrong figure. Real transactions also add spreads or fees not included here.

name: VAT amount
description: Calculates the value-added tax on a net (pre-tax) amount by multiplying it by the VAT rate. The result is the tax due, which is added to the net amount to reach the gross price.
notes: Applies to the net amount, not the gross. Rate is a decimal (0.10 = 10%). To back out VAT from a gross price instead, divide the gross by (1 + rate) first.

name: Sales tax amount
description: Computes the sales tax owed by multiplying a pre-tax price by the tax rate. The result is the added tax amount that a buyer pays on top of the listed price.
notes: Applies to the pre-tax price and rate is a decimal (0.10 = 10%). If a price already includes tax, this overstates the tax; extract it with price/(1 + rate) instead.

name: Gross Margin from Markup
description: Converts a markup (profit as a fraction of cost) into gross margin (profit as a percent of selling price) via markup/(1+markup)×100. A 0.5 markup corresponds to a 33.33% gross margin.
notes: Markup is entered as a fraction, not a percent, so 50% markup is 0.5. Markup and margin are not the same figure; markup always exceeds the equivalent margin.

name: Markup from Margin
description: Converts a gross margin (profit as a fraction of selling price) into the equivalent markup on cost via margin/(1-margin)×100. A 0.3 margin corresponds to a 42.86% markup.
notes: Margin is entered as a fraction between 0 and 1, not a percent. As margin approaches 1 the required markup rises steeply toward infinity.

name: Selling Price from Cost & Margin
description: Computes the selling price needed to achieve a target gross margin from a unit cost, using cost/(1-margin). At a cost of 100 and a 0.4 target margin the price is 166.67.
notes: Margin is a fraction of the selling price, not of cost, and must be below 1. Simply adding the margin percentage to cost would understate the required price.

name: Split the bill
description: Divides a total amount equally among a number of people, computing total÷people. The result is each person's equal share.
notes: This splits the total evenly; it does not handle unequal shares or added tips. The number of people must be nonzero.

name: Wage (rate × hours)
description: Computes gross pay as hourly rate×hours worked. The result is the total earnings before any deductions such as tax.
notes: This is gross pay, before tax or other deductions, and does not include overtime premiums unless those hours are entered separately.

name: Price before tax
description: Recovers the pre-tax price from a tax-included total by dividing the total by (1 + rate/100). It isolates the base amount before the given tax rate was added.
notes: Enter the tax rate as a percentage (e.g. 10 for 10%). This is not the same as simply subtracting the rate from the total, which overstates the deduction.

name: Total with tip and tax
description: Computes a final bill by applying tax and then tip multiplicatively to the base amount: bill × (1 + tax/100) × (1 + tip/100). Both rates are compounded onto the bill.
notes: Tip here is applied on the tax-inclusive amount because of the multiplication order. Enter tax and tip as percentages; applying tip on the pre-tax bill gives a lower total.

name: Stacked discount price
description: Applies two successive percentage discounts to a price: price × (1 − d1/100) × (1 − d2/100). The second discount is taken on the already-reduced amount.
notes: Stacked discounts do not add up; 20% then 10% is a 28% total reduction, not 30%. Enter each discount as a percentage.

name: Unit price
description: Calculates the price per single item by dividing the total price by the quantity. It lets you compare value across packs of different sizes.
notes: Both price and quantity must use consistent units; the result is cost per one unit. A lower unit price means better value for the same product.

name: Currency with fee
description: Converts a foreign-currency amount into local currency and deducts a percentage fee, using amount × rate × (1 − fee/100). It gives the net amount received after conversion charges.
notes: Enter the fee as a percentage of the converted value. Real providers may add fixed charges or a spread in the rate, so the actual amount can be lower.

name: Hourly to annual salary
description: Estimates an annual salary from an hourly wage as rate × hours per week × 52 weeks in a year.
notes: Assumes 52 paid weeks with no unpaid time off; holidays, sick leave, and taxes are not deducted. It is a gross, pre-tax figure.

name: Annual to hourly rate
description: Converts an annual salary to an equivalent hourly rate by dividing it by hours per week × 52 weeks.
notes: Uses 52 weeks of work per year and does not account for paid leave or taxes. The result is a gross hourly figure before deductions.

name: Overtime pay
description: Calculates overtime pay as the hourly rate multiplied by a 1.25 premium and by the number of overtime hours worked.
notes: Assumes a 25% overtime premium; actual multipliers vary by law and contract (e.g. 1.35 for late-night or holiday work in Japan). Adjust the factor accordingly.

name: Net pay after tax
description: Computes take-home pay from gross pay by subtracting a deduction percentage, using gross × (1 − tax/100).
notes: Enter the combined deduction rate as a percentage. Real payroll uses progressive brackets and separate items (tax, pension, insurance), so a single flat rate is an approximation.

name: Tip per person
description: Calculates each person's share of the tip by taking the tip percentage of the bill and dividing it among the people, using bill × tip/100 / people.
notes: This splits only the tip, not the bill itself; enter the tip as a percentage. Assumes the tip is shared equally among all people.

name: Meeting cost
description: Estimates the labor cost of a meeting as the number of participants × each person's hourly cost × the meeting duration in hours.
notes: Assumes every participant shares the same hourly cost; use a blended average if rates differ. Captures only staff time, not overhead or opportunity cost.

name: Electricity cost
description: Calculates the cost of electricity by multiplying the energy consumed in kilowatt-hours by the unit price per kilowatt-hour.
notes: Uses a single flat unit price and excludes fixed base charges, fuel adjustments, and tiered rates that appear on real bills.

name: Water bill
description: Estimates a water bill as the volume used in cubic meters × the unit price, plus a fixed base charge.
notes: Assumes a single flat volumetric rate; many utilities use tiered pricing and add sewage charges separately. Base charge is added once.

name: Split cost evenly
description: Divides a total amount by the number of people to give each person's equal share of the bill. The result is the amount one person pays when the cost is split evenly.
notes: The result is rounded to whole units, so rounding may leave the sum of shares slightly above or below the true total. People must be a positive count.

name: Real Hourly Wage
description: Divides take-home pay minus the costs of working by all the hours the job really takes (from Your Money or Your Life).
notes: Useful to judge purchases in hours of life.

name: Effective Discount of "Buy X Get Y Free"
description: Gives the equivalent percentage discount of a buy-x-get-y-free offer.
notes: "Buy 2 get 1 free" is a 33.3 % discount, not 50 %.

name: Bill Split with Tip
description: Divides a bill plus tip equally among a group.
notes: Round up to a convenient amount if paying cash.

name: Currency Conversion after Fee
description: Converts money at a quoted rate and deducts the provider's fee or spread.
notes: Card and airport rates often hide 2–5 % in the spread.

name: Emergency Fund Target
description: Gives the cash reserve for a chosen number of months of essential spending.
notes: Three to six months is the usual advice; more for irregular incomes.

name: Savings Rate
description: Gives the share of take-home income that is saved.
notes: The single biggest driver of how soon financial independence is reached.

name: Price per Unit Comparison (Savings of the Bigger Pack)
description: Compares unit prices and gives how much cheaper per unit the second pack is.
notes: Negative means the "bigger" pack is actually more expensive per unit.

name: Net Amount from a VAT-Inclusive Price
description: Removes value-added tax (or GST) from a tax-inclusive price.
notes: Do not simply subtract 20 %: 120 incl. 20 % VAT is 100 net, not 96.

name: VAT Contained in a Gross Price
description: Gives the amount of tax inside a tax-inclusive price.
notes: At 20 % the tax is one sixth of the gross price.

name: Gross-Up for a Net Amount
description: Gives the gross payment needed so that a given amount is left after tax is withheld.
notes: Used for bonuses, royalties and cross-border payments.

name: Progressive Tax by Brackets
expression: sum(k, 1, len(lim), max(min(inc, at(lim, k)) - if(k == 1, 0, at(lim, k - 1)), 0) * at(rt, k))
description: Computes tax under a progressive schedule in which each slice of income is taxed at the rate of its own bracket.
notes: Enter your own country's brackets; the defaults are only an illustration. Moving into a higher bracket never lowers take-home pay.

name: Effective and Marginal Tax Rate Gap
description: Shows how far the average (effective) tax rate is below the rate on the last unit of income.
notes: Decisions about extra work or deductions depend on the marginal rate, not the average.

name: Real Return after Tax and Inflation
description: Gives the growth of purchasing power after taxes on the nominal return and inflation.
notes: Tax on the inflation part makes real after-tax returns small or negative.

name: Vehicle Cost per Kilometre
description: Gives the total cost of owning and running a vehicle per kilometre driven.
notes: Useful for comparing cars, car-sharing and public transport.
